name: Morok Metpa
instructions: 1. Roast the green chilies and onions over an open flame until charred or steam them until soft.
2. In a mortar and pestle, grind the fermented fish (Ngari) into a paste.
3. Add the roasted chilies and onions to the mortar and mash them together with the fish paste.
4. Add a boiled and peeled potato to the mixture and mash until well combined but slightly textured.
5. Season with salt to taste and garnish with fresh coriander leaves before serving.
description: Morok Metpa is a staple side dish in Manipuri cuisine. Its name translates to 'chili mash' (Morok meaning chili and Metpa meaning mash). It is a pungent, fiery, and flavorful accompaniment served with steamed rice and Eromba, embodying the authentic, bold flavors of Northeast Indian culinary traditions.
